abilities.name: Nightrider

_curatorNotes: icdGate authored 2026-08-17 (ICD-group round b): gcsim skill.go:145 sets ICDGroupFischl on the Oz tick, whose table entry (pkg/core/attacks/icd_groups.dm.go) is a 300f reset window with every 4th hit applying inside it. Measured 3/10 applied against standard ICD's 4. ⚓ This is the series docs/icd-group-round.md §3 prices the whole sub-landing on — 8 oracle applications across both Ozes, and the ONE genuinely-group row in that residue.

effects.attribution: A4: Undone Be Thy Sinful Hex
_curatorNotes: icdGate 'none' authored 2026-08-18 (coordinated-attack round): gcsim fischl/asc.go:51 sets ICDTagNone on Thundering Retribution, so every proc applies its full gauge. ⚠️ Authored rather than left absent because absent now means STANDARD ICD for a proc, as it always has for a summon tick — before the gate existed this effect was ungated by omission, and the round made the omission mean something else.

Coordinated attack, authored 2026-08-18. gcsim fischl/fischl.go:61 registers a minazuki.Watcher on action.NormalAttackState with tickerFreq 60 and NO ICD key, gated on ozActiveKey and firing c6Wave (cons.go) — Electro, Durability 25, ICDTagElementalArt/ICDGroupFischl, landing at ozTravel (10f), Mult 0.3 = 30% of Fischl's ATK.

icdGate is ICDGroupFischl verbatim (300f timer, every 4th), the same window Oz's own tick series carries. ⚠️ In gcsim the wave and Oz's ticks share ONE counter — same tag AND group — while ours are two, because an ICD counter here is keyed per listener/series. Ours therefore applies slightly more often at C6 than gcsim does; the alternative is a cross-series shared-counter key for one constellation case.

⚠️ gcsim's watcher passes an EMPTY icd key, so in gcsim every re-entry into the normal-attack state fires a wave regardless of how recently the last one landed. Ours gates entries on the interval like the other three. It shows only under rapid dash-cancel re-entry.

Oz tick: gcsim ozTickInterval=59f (=0.983s), firstTick=64f post-spawn (=1.067s). Multiplier birdAtk at TalentLvl 10 = 159.84% ATK Electro. Per-tick damage authored as a `summonTick` effect on the summon (P3); the timeline renders one marker per tick on the summon bar.
A6 rigor 2026-07-12: scaling corrected 247.32 → 159.84 (gcsim birdAtk[9]=1.5984; genshin-db sidecar Oz's ATK DMG L10 159.8%). Prior 247.32 matched no Fischl multiplier at any level.

↻ firstTickDelay +10f on BOTH Ozes, 2026-09-16 (T0.5) — every tick marker was 10 frames early. gcsim queues each tick's damage with `c.ozTravel` (fischl.go:39, default 10) as the attack delay: `ozTick` fires at spawn + firstTick and then calls QueueAttackEvent(&ae, c.ozTravel), so the skill Oz's first DAMAGE lands at 18 + 64 + 10 = 92f and the burst Oz's at 1 + 63 + 10 = 74f. We authored the pre-travel 64f / 63f. New values 1.233 (74f) and 1.217 (73f) — measured against the frames report's own side-by-side, ours 82f vs gcsim 92f. The interval is untouched, so the whole series shifts by the travel time, which is what it does in game.

⚠️⚠️ THE TICK COUNT IS ONE SHORT AT THE BOUNDARY AND `tickCap` IS THE WRONG FIX — TRIED, MEASURED, REVERTED 2026-09-16. Pushing the series 10 frames later for the travel time cost the last tick: `Fischl E` is 9 markers at C0 and 11 at C6 where gcsim gives 10 and 12, and the regenerated frames report flags it outright ("count 9→10"). gcsim gates the TASK, not the damage — ozTick checks ozActiveKey at 82 + 59k, all ten inside the 600f status, and only then queues the damage at +10, so its last hit lands at 623 with the status already closed at 618. That is the boundary case tickCap exists for, and `tickCap: 10` + `tickCapScaling: 12` does produce 10 and 12.

⛔ It was reverted because the cap widens the window by ONE WHOLE INTERVAL (`limit = endAt + s.interval`, summons.ts), and Oz's window is routinely TRUNCATED by the burst recast — which is Fischl's standard rotation. Measured `Fischl E Q`: the skill Oz runs 18→44f and the cap let its first tick through at 92, a marker 48 frames PAST the end of its own bar, which `computeSummonSubrows` passes to the renderer unclipped. A visibly wrong pixel on the common rotation is worse than a missing one at the boundary of the rare uninterrupted one. ⏭ The engine nuance is that the one-interval widening is right for a NATURAL end and wrong for a truncated one; the walk cannot currently tell them apart.

abilities.description:
Summons Oz to spread his twin wings of twilight and defend Fischl.
Has the following properties during the ability's duration:
·Fischl takes on Oz's form, greatly increasing her Movement Speed.
·Strikes nearby opponents with lightning, dealing Electro DMG to opponents she comes into contact with. Each opponent can only be struck once.
·Once this ability's effects end, Oz will remain on the battlefield and attack his Prinzessin's foes. If Oz is already on the field, then this will reset the duration of his presence.

passives.name: Undone Be Thy Sinful Hex
passives.description: If your current active character triggers an Electro-related Elemental Reaction when Oz is on the field, the opponent shall be stricken with Thundering Retribution that deals Electro DMG equal to 80% of Fischl's ATK.
_curatorNotes: MODELLED 2026-08-17 as a damage effect on an onReaction trigger, authored on OZ (both the skill's and the burst's summon) rather than here — the summon's own liveness is the "when Oz is on the field" gate, so no armedFor is needed. 80% ATK, Electro, 1U (Durability 25, ICDTagNone), 4 frames after the reaction, 0.5s ICD. Reaction list from asc.go's subscriptions: OnOverload, OnElectroCharged, OnSuperconduct, OnSwirlElectro, OnCrystallizeElectro, OnHyperbloom, OnQuicken, OnAggravate — plus stellarConduct, which replaces superConduct team-wide when an enabler is present. OnLunarCharged is omitted: we do not emit lunarCharged at all, so authoring it would be inert.

⚠️ source 'active' is what makes this RIGHT WHERE GCSIM IS WRONG, and the oracle should not be used to judge it. gcsim gates on ae.Info.ActorIndex != Player.Active(), and Oz's attacks carry Fischl's actor index — so with Fischl on field, Oz's own reactions pass the check. Measured in docs/curation/gcsim-reaction-diff.md's quicken fixture, EVERY Thundering Retribution gcsim emits lands exactly 4 frames after an Oz application, i.e. every one of them is a proc the game does not make. Our source 'active' refuses an application delivered by an entity, so those do not fire here and the oracle will keep reporting them missing. That is the correct outcome.

Two divergences kept small and deliberate: gcsim stores the 0.5s ICD on the ACTIVE character (so a swap refreshes it) while ours is per-effect, and A4's snapshot is Oz's rather than Fischl's current stats — neither affects elemental application, which is all this feeds today.

In practice Oz's ~1s attack cadence frequently steals the electro reaction before the active character can make it, making reliable activation highly aura-dependent; off-field-Fischl compositions rarely benefit.

↻ CAVEAT REMOVED 2026-08-18 (caveat refresh): STALE — both claims are now working behavior. The A4 proc is authored on BOTH Ozes as a damage effect on {onReaction, source:`active`, icdGate:`none`}; `source:active` refuses an offer carrying viaEntity, which is exactly the "Oz`s own reactions do not count" rule. See docs/mark-triggered-damage-round.md.

factionBonuses.name: Secret Rite
factionBonuses.description: When 2+ Hexerei members are in the team, triggering an Electro reaction grants ATK% (overloaded) or EM (electroCharged / lunarCharged) to self and active character for 10s.
_curatorNotes: ↻ `duringSummon` ADDED to both gates, 2026-09-16 (T0.5) — and ⚠️⚠️ MEASURED INERT TODAY, which is why this note exists. gcsim asc.go:135-160: both the atkpHook and the emHook `return` when !StatusIsActive(ozActiveKey), so the Secret Rite needs Oz ON THE FIELD and ours drew off any Electro reaction Fischl triggered, Oz long gone. The condition is correct data about the mechanic, but a `state` gate is UNRESOLVABLE on the reaction buff pass and the projection drops only a definitive false — measured `Fischl E A ~13s > Klee E N1 N2 N3 > Fischl A A`: Oz dies at 10.30s and the 22.48s Overload still draws a 22.48→32.48s +22.5% ATK bar, before AND after this edit. ⛔ So don't read it as handled. It starts working the day §1.G (resolved states in the buff projections) lands, and until then the divergence is narrow: it needs Fischl herself to trigger an Electro reaction with Oz down, and her normals are Physical.

⛔ No caveat for it: lint E.28 refuses a caveat on a factionBonus effect, and the nearest ability-shaped host is the skill, where an entry about a faction bonus would be reading the wrong label. Filed here instead.

↻ RESOLVED (state-gates round §1.G, 2026-09-19 — `docs/state-gates-round.md`): the reaction buff pass reads Fischl's `duringSummon` at the reaction. Measured `Bennett E > Fischl C` (no Oz): the +22.5% ATK bar no longer draws; under Oz it draws per Overload as before.
